newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends higher on funds, export rumors.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends higher on funds, export rumors.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed higher on Wednesday, boosted by fund buying and ideas of export business in the works, traders said.
Soymeal ended mixed with new crop months down amid talk China bought South American supplies.

Floor sources cited rumors Taiwan was looking to buy soyoil. They said Taiwan normally bought soybeans to crush into soymeal and soyoil but a cut in Taiwan's hog herd due to foot and mouth disease, had sliced demand for soymeal.
Chartists said technicals were bullish in the soyoil pit but soymeal continued to give off bearish indications.

Some trade sources also noted expectations that Thursday's U.S. Census Bureau report would reflect a dip in soyoil and soymeal stockpiles. Soyoil stocks were at 2.202 million lbs and soymeal at 165,278 tons in the March 27 report

Soymeal futures were pressured by talk China this week bought 200,000 tonnes of South American soymeal, adding to rumors China last week bought 150,000 tonnes of soymeal from South America, traders said.
Soymeal closed $1.00 a ton higher to $0.70 lower with May down $0.10 at $272.40. Soyoil closed 0.40 to 0.20 cent per lb higher with May up 0.27 at 24.93.

On the day, Rosenthal Collins bought 800 lots July soyoil, Merrill Lynch bought 500 July, R.J. O'Brien bought 400 July and Prudential Securities and Griffin Trading each bought 300 July, pit sources said.
In soymeal, ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp sold 700 lots July and Merrill Lynch sold 200 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 18,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 21,935 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 18,000 lots, against Tuesday's 15,378.
